## The rows

| id | status | where | text | rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ctrl.label` | NEW | describe door — a new row directly below the KB picker's <label> | Filling in a template? | A QUESTION, not a noun. The KB picker above it already asks a question ('Which knowledge base should this use?'); a bare 'Template' label would read as a third field to fill rather than an optional branch. It must also be ignorable at a glance — SC#4 says the fast door stays fast. |
| `ctrl.note` | NEW | describe door — sub-note under ctrl.label | Attach the document this should fill in — the draft is built to its fields. | States the CONSEQUENCE, which is the whole reason the phase exists: attaching changes what gets drafted. Without this sentence the control reads as a file upload that happens early, and SEED-157's defect (a draft built blind) survives with a control on screen. |
| `ctrl.button` | NEW | describe door — the file input's label | Attach a template | ⚠ DELIBERATELY THE SHIPPED `TEMPLATE_ATTACH_LABEL` STRING, character for character. Two doors onto the same act must not have two names for it. If this phase changes the word, it changes it in `TemplateAttachSection.tsx` and both move. |
| `ctrl.types` | SHIPPED | TemplateAttachSection.tsx — TEMPLATE_TYPES_NOTE | Word, PowerPoint or Excel — .docx, .pptx or .xlsx, up to 10 MB. | Inherited verbatim. The accepted set is a server rule; a second copy of it here would be free to drift from the gate that actually refuses (D-182-06). |
| `spec.heading` | SHIPPED | TemplateAttachSection.tsx — TEMPLATE_FIELDS_HEADING | What this template asks for | Inherited verbatim. This heading already ships on the rail; the pre-draft screen showing the SAME words for the same list is what makes the two surfaces read as one fact rather than two features. |
| `spec.promise` | NEW | describe door — one line under the fields list (variants B and C) | The draft will be built to fill these 8 fields. | ⚠ THE ONE SENTENCE THAT MAKES SC#2 VISIBLE. Everything else on this screen says what the TEMPLATE contains; only this says what the DRAFT will be aimed at. ⚠ It states a COUNT, so it must be derived from the list rendered above it and never hardcoded — a '8' beside a list of 5 is the exact class of silent lie SEED-157 is about. |
| `spec.filenameLead` | NEW | describe door — variant C's spec-block header, before the filename | Drafting to | C only. Names the relationship rather than restating the file: the rail's own `📄 filename` line answers 'what is attached', this answers 'what is it FOR'. |
| `hint.withTemplate` | CHANGE | testid="describe-hint" — replaces the three-fragment sentence WHEN a template is attached | The AI writes the steps that gather what these fields need — then you review what it chose. | ⚠ A CHANGE TO A GOVERNED STRING. The shipped hint is composed of three `<b>` fragments carried in `doorVocabulary.ts` and pinned byte-exact by `WorkflowBuilderPage.describe.test.tsx`. Replacing it conditionally means a SECOND sentence in that module and a second pinned capture — it is not a copy edit, and it is called out here so planning prices it. If the phase declines it, the shipped sentence stays and this row is dropped: the screen still works, it just promises less. |
| `cta.withTemplate` | SHIPPED | testid="describe-draft" | Write the first draft | ⚠ DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, and this is a decision rather than an omission. The button does the same thing whether or not a template is attached; a second verb ('Draft to this template') would suggest a second code path to a user who has one path. What changed is the INPUT, and the input is what the screen above the button now shows. |
